top_stories.title: Uk Gurdwara Alliance: 'They speak only for themselves': UK Sikh group distance community from social media commentators Harman Kapoor, Bobby Singh | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The UK Gurdwara Alliance** issued a statement clarifying that social media commentators **Harman Kapoor** and **Bobby Singh** do not represent the Sikh community or any recognised Sikh representative body. The organizations emphasized that views expressed by these individuals should be considered personal opinions rather than official positions of the wider Sikh community, urging media outlets to avoid portraying them as representatives of Sikh views.  The clarification aims to prevent misrepresentation of the Sikh community and protect the integrity of Sikh institutions and collective decision-making processes.

top_stories.title: A 2200-year-old Chinese four-lane highway discovered buried in the mountains, revealing a lost Qin dynasty megaproject | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in northwest China's Shaanxi province have uncovered a 13-kilometer stretch of the Qin Straight Road, an ancient imperial artery built over 2,200 years ago. The discovery, made during a survey led by the **Cultural Heritage Protection and Research Institute of Yulin**, reveals evidence of engineered road construction techniques, including rammed-earth slope reinforcements, compacted roadbeds, trench-style passes, and valleys deliberately filled to maintain alignment. This new segment reinforces historical accounts suggesting that the Qin Straight Road was not built for lane discipline but for parallel movement, facilitating military columns, supply carts, mounted couriers, and administrative convoys within a controlled corridor.  The discovery sheds light on the ambitious engineering project undertaken by the **Qin dynasty** during the reign of **Qin Shi Huang**.

top_stories.title: Japan just switched on Asia’s first osmotic power plant and it runs on seawater and sewage | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: A desalination plant in Japan has become the world's second osmotic power plant, generating electricity from a continuous flow of fresh water and saltwater. The facility, located at the Uminonakamichi Nata Seawater Desalination Centre, utilizes concentrated brine waste from the desalination process and treated wastewater to create power. While the output is modest, the plant offers near-total reliability as it operates continuously regardless of weather conditions. This approach avoids the need for expensive membrane breakthroughs and leverages readily available resources, marking a pragmatic solution for scaling osmotic power generation.

top_stories.title: 77 headless skeletons unearthed in Europe’s most mysterious Neolithic burial site in Slovakia | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Archaeologists** working in western Slovakia have uncovered a Neolithic settlement ditch containing at least 77 headless human skeletons, dating back to roughly 5250-4950 BC. The remains suggest coordinated decapitation and disposal, but the meticulous arrangement of the bodies in clusters rather than random deposition complicates this interpretation.  The study published in Cambridge University Journals suggests that the heads were likely removed after death, possibly for ritualistic purposes or as part of a community-wide practice.

top_stories.title: Amnesty International Warns That World Cup Fans Face Potential Human Rights Violations | WIRED
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Amnesty International** warns that millions attending the 2026 FIFA World Cup in **the United States, Mexico, and Canada** face risks to their human rights. The organization highlights a "human rights emergency" characterized by racial profiling and mass detentions by agencies like **Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)** and **Customs and Border Protection (CBP)** in the US. In Mexico, the deployment of 100,000 security agents, including members of the army, increases risks for peaceful demonstrations.  **Amnesty International** also expresses concerns about housing issues in Canada potentially displacing unhoused populations during the tournament.

top_stories.title: FACT, Chambal Fertilisers shares up to 5% as government eyes doubling fertiliser subsidy allocation - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Agriculture** has requested the **Finance Ministry** to double the fertilizer subsidy allocation to Rs 1.71 lakh crore, citing escalating global fertilizer prices and import costs. This proposal comes amidst disruptions linked to the ongoing West Asia conflict, which has strained global supply chains and increased fertilizer prices. Officials warn that if these challenges persist, India's fertilizer subsidy bill could exceed Rs 3 lakh crore this fiscal year. However, domestic production improvements may ease the burden somewhat.  The prospect of higher subsidy support and sustained demand optimism has made the sector a standout performer in Wednesday's trade.

top_stories.title: Trump says Iran military is a 'complete mess' after US strikes; warns Tehran to 'pay the price'
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** issued a warning to **Iran**, calling its military "a complete and total mess" after US retaliatory strikes.  He blamed the crash of a US Army helicopter on the Islamic Republic, stating that Iran is "all talk and no action." The exchange of hostilities followed Israeli-Iranian attacks earlier this week, escalating Middle East tensions. **Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu** reiterated Israel's opposition to Iran's nuclear program, defending its past strikes against Tehran.

top_stories.title: Indian-origin billionaire announces Dh1m aid for UAE road crash victims: 6 Indians among 7 dead | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Dr Shamsheer Vayalil**, a billionaire Indian-origin businessman and philanthropist, announced a Dh1 million humanitarian support package for families affected by the recent Emirates Road crash. The initiative will provide financial assistance to the families of the seven deceased workers, totaling Dh700,000, as well as medical treatment and recovery funds for the nine injured survivors.  The package also includes support for emergency travel and accommodation costs, education expenses, and other needs for affected families. **Dr Vayalil**, founder and chairman of **Burjeel Holdings**, a leading healthcare group in the Middle East, stated that the assistance aims to provide immediate relief and ease the burden on grieving families while helping injured workers recover.

top_stories.title: Trump says Iran military is a 'complete mess' after US strikes; warns Tehran to 'pay the price'
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** warned **Iran**'s military is a "complete and total mess" after the US launched retaliatory strikes, blaming the crash of a US Army helicopter on Tehran.  He also hailed the US naval blockade of **Iran**, calling it a "steel wall" that has crippled Iran's economy. **Benjamin Netanyahu**, Israeli Prime Minister, reiterated his opposition to **Iran**'s nuclear program and defended Israel's past attacks on **Tehran**.

top_stories.title: Concord Biotech shares gain 6% after USFDA approval for Tofacitinib tablets - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Concord Biotech** announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of its ANDA for Tofacitinib Tablets, indicated for treating various inflammatory conditions like rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, ankylosing spondylitis, ulcerative colitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. The company expects this approval to strengthen its presence in the U.S. market and expand its product portfolio, with an estimated $500 million market opportunity for the two approved dosage strengths.  The approval aligns with **Concord Biotech's** growth strategy and supports its long-term plans.
